# Researcher — mathematical essay / blog post

You are a researcher writing a mathematical essay or technical blog post explaining **P-FDT (policy functional decision theory)** and how to apply it to decision problems.

Your intended readers are mathematically literate and interested in both the formal procedure and its philosophical motivation.

Read the human-written reference article supplied below carefully. Write your own coherent account of the theory, with mathematical definitions, equations, examples, and explanations to whatever extent you find useful. Aim for a precise enough understanding that a reader could use your essay to decide unfamiliar cases.

Explain how the theory evaluates alternative actions or policies and how it treats relevant dependencies and counterfactuals. Where the source leaves an important question open, explain the uncertainty and, if you think a reasonable operational interpretation is available, develop and justify it. Distinguish claims made by the source from additional assumptions or proposals of your own.

Write the result as a substantive, readable mathematical essay rather than an answer to one assigned case. Use examples whenever they help explain the theory.

Target approximately 2,400–3,000 words, including references and any other material. Prioritize a coherent, complete explanation of the central definitions, reasoning, and important implications over exhaustive coverage. Avoid unnecessary repetition, lengthy bibliographies, and appendices. Finish with a brief conclusion.

For this essay, explain **policy functional decision theory (P-FDT)**. Take the **policy-selection passage in footnote 16** of the supplied paper as the primary source for P-FDT in this assignment. Use **P-FDT** consistently as the assigned decision theory's name, including in headings and examples, and identify any other decision theory you discuss by its distinct name. Keep quotations faithful to the source. Explain your best mathematical understanding of P-FDT and how it can be applied. Where the footnote leaves choices unresolved, explain those uncertainties and any additional assumptions you find appropriate. The aim is your interpretation of the source, not a predetermined completion.


## Human-written reference

Title: Functional Decision Theory: A New Theory of Instrumental Rationality

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/src/1710.05060v2
